latin.2578: CXLI. Ne tamen quaedam paginae hic vacent, summatim adjiciemus, quasi exempli causa, sententiam Gregorii de Valentia Jesuitae satis nobilis, quam plures viri docti referunt & refutant. Ille igitur existimat gratiam efficacem consistere in aliquo dono, quod homo jam praeventus a gratia vocante & excitante, possit cum auxilio Dei consequi, per pium usum sui liberi arbitrii: quodque in uno genere causae, scilicet efficientis, sit natura prius quam ipsa libera conversio; & in alio posterius, scilicet in genere causae materialis atque dispositivae.
latin.2579: CXLII. Hoc autem donum consistere vult in infusione habituum gratiae ac virtutum: quatenus per eos habitus mens hominis roborata elicit actum conversionis. Adeoque secundum ejus opinionem, gratia efficax aut est gratia habitualis, quum infunditur, aut ipsa ejus infusio: quatenus scilicet, per illam gratiam infusam liberum arbitrium elicit suam ipsius conversionem, Deo simul ad eam concurrente.
latin.2580: CXLIII. Ut vero aliquis censeatur habere sufficientem gratiam ad piam actionem, ex ejus sententia, necesse est ut habeat, aut omnia dona & auxilia, quae ad actionem tanquam illius principia, sive initia requiruntur, aut sic aliquod vel aliqua ex hujusmodi donis, ut per illud vel illa jam praeventus & excitatus, possit usu aliquo liberae facultatis suae, auxiliante Deo, acquirere reliqua omnia ejusmodi dona sive auxilia. Ut videre est apud jam dictum Gregorium tom. 2. disputat. 8. quaest. 3. punct. 4.
latin.2581: CXLIV. Unde patet hunc Doctorem nolle eandem esse entitatem realem gratiae sufficientis, & gratiae efficacis; sed gratiam efficacem novum auxilium ad sufficientem addere, quod conversionem hominis praeveniat: qua in re ad Thomistas recentiores accedit, & dissentit a Molina, & authoribus gratiae congruae: Et simul tamen eum nolle efficaciam gratiae divinae esse absolutam, sed pendere ab usu liberi nostri arbitrii, qua in re deserit Thomistas, & ad Theologos istos posteriores accedit.
latin.2582: CXLV. In ejus vero sententia hoc peculiare incommodum occurrit, quod quae de gratia efficaci dicit, in sola peccatoris ad Deum conversione locum habere possint, non vero in bonis operibus hominis jam conversi; ad quae nulla requiritur nova habitualis gratiae infusio, & ad quae tamen gratia efficax se extendit. Ac praeterea mihi quidem intelligibile non est, quomodo infusio gratiae habitualis possit esse hominis conversione prior in genere causae efficientis, & simul tamen eadem conversione posterior in genere causae dispositivae.

sections.title: Appendix: Gregory of Valencia on efficacious grace
sections.pass_a: CXLI. Yet lest some pages be empty here, we will add in summary, as it were by way of example, the opinion of Gregory of Valencia a Jesuit of sufficient note, which several learned men report & refute. He then thinks that efficacious grace consists in some gift, which a man already prevented by calling & rousing grace, can obtain with the help of God, through the pious use of his free choice: and which in one genus of cause, namely efficient, is prior by nature to the free conversion itself; & in another posterior, namely in the genus of material and dispositive cause.
pass_b: Thesis CXLI. So that some pages are not left blank here, we will add in brief, as an example, the opinion of Gregory of Valencia, a Jesuit of some note, which a number of learned men report and refute. He holds that efficacious grace consists in a gift that a person already forestalled by calling and stirring grace can obtain, with God's help, through devout use of his free choice. In one order of cause, the efficient, this gift is by nature prior to the free conversion itself; in another, the material and dispositive, it is posterior.

sections.title: The gift: infused habits of grace and the virtues
sections.pass_a: CXLII. And this gift he will have consist in the infusion of habits of grace and of the virtues: inasmuch as through those habits the mind of man being strengthened elicits the act of conversion. And so according to his opinion, efficacious grace is either habitual grace, when it is infused, or its infusion itself: inasmuch namely as, through that infused grace free choice elicits its own conversion, God concurring at the same time to it.
pass_b: Thesis CXLII. He places this gift in the infusion of habits of grace and of the virtues, since the human mind, strengthened by those habits, elicits the act of conversion. On his view, then, efficacious grace is either habitual grace as it is infused, or the infusion itself, insofar as through that infused grace free choice elicits its own conversion, with God concurring in it at the same time.

sections.title: Valencia on sufficient grace
sections.pass_a: CXLIII. But for someone to be judged to have sufficient grace for a pious action, in his opinion, it is necessary that he have, either all the gifts & aids, which are required for the action as its principles, or beginnings, or so some one or some of gifts of this kind, that through it or them already prevented & roused, he can by some use of his free faculty, God assisting, acquire all the rest of such gifts or aids. As may be seen in the aforesaid Gregory tom. 2. disputat. 8. quaest. 3. punct. 4.
pass_b: Thesis CXLIII. On his view, for someone to count as having sufficient grace for a devout action, he must have either all the gifts and aids that the action requires as its principles or starting points, or else one or more of those gifts, such that, forestalled and stirred by it or them, he can acquire all the remaining gifts or aids of that kind through some use of his free faculty, with God's help. This can be seen in Gregory, already named, tome 2, disputation 8, question 3, point 4.

sections.title: Between the Thomists and the later theologians
sections.pass_a: CXLIV. Whence it is clear that this Doctor will not have the real entity of sufficient grace, & of efficacious grace be the same; but that efficacious grace adds a new aid to the sufficient, which precedes the conversion of the man: in which matter he approaches the recent Thomists, & dissents from Molina, & the authors of congruous grace: And at the same time however that he will not have the efficacy of divine grace be absolute, but depend on the use of our free choice, in which matter he deserts the Thomists, & approaches those later Theologians.
pass_b: Thesis CXLIV. Clearly, then, this doctor denies that sufficient and efficacious grace are the same real entity. Efficacious grace, for him, adds to sufficient grace a new aid that comes before the person's conversion; here he sides with the recent Thomists and parts from Molina and the authors of congruous grace.

Yet at the same time he denies that the efficacy of divine grace is absolute, making it depend instead on the use of our free choice; here he leaves the Thomists and sides with those later theologians.

sections.title: Le Blanc's objections to Valencia
sections.pass_a: CXLV. But in his opinion this peculiar difficulty occurs, that what he says of efficacious grace, can have place only in the conversion of the sinner to God, but not in the good works of a man already converted; for which no new infusion of habitual grace is required, & to which nevertheless efficacious grace extends itself. And besides to me indeed it is not intelligible, how the infusion of habitual grace can be prior to the man's conversion in the genus of efficient cause, & at the same time nevertheless posterior to the same conversion in the genus of dispositive cause.
pass_b: Thesis CXLV. His opinion runs into a difficulty of its own: what he says about efficacious grace can apply only to the sinner's conversion to God, not to the good works of someone already converted. Those works need no new infusion of habitual grace, and yet efficacious grace extends to them as well.

Besides, for my part I cannot understand how the infusion of habitual grace can be prior to a person's conversion as efficient cause and yet at the same time posterior to that same conversion as dispositive cause.
